item.title: AWS extends Trusted Identity Propagation to IAM Federation and Roles Anywhere
item.description:
AWS extends Trusted Identity Propagation to IAM Federation and Roles Anywhere

AWS has extended Trusted Identity Propagation (TIP) to support IAM federation and AWS IAM Roles Anywhere, enabling customers to grant access and audit activity based on the specific user or workload behind an IAM role.

🔍 Overview

Trusted Identity Propagation (TIP) carries the identity of a user or workload with each AWS request. This allows users to grant permissions to that specific user or workload and trace its actions in AWS CloudTrail. Previously, TIP was available only for users accessing AWS through AWS IAM Identity Center. The new extension makes TIP work for users and workloads that federate directly into IAM roles or use X.509 certificates to obtain AWS credentials, while also simplifying TIP usage with IAM Identity Center.

🧩 How it works

TIP addresses the gap where access control decisions apply to the role rather than the user, and CloudTrail attributes each action to the role session. By attaching identity context from a trusted source to the role session at credential issuance, TIP provides a stable reference for the user or workload behind each request. This context is immutable for the lifetime of the session and can include optional claims, such as a risk score or a CI/CD workflow name.

The identity context propagates through supported downstream requests:

  • Role Assumption: When a TIP session assumes another role, AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) carries the context into the new role session.
  • Forward Access Sessions (FAS): When an AWS service makes a downstream request on your behalf, FAS credentials carry the identity context.
  • Outbound Federation: With IAM outbound identity federation, the session can request a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) that carries identity context to an external service.

⚙️ Key details

AWS validates the source and attaches identity context through three primary paths:

Path Source of Identity Context Trusted Source Type
IAM Federation SAML assertion or OIDC token External SAML or OIDC Identity Providers (IdP)
IAM Identity Center Username received from identity source IAM Identity Center
IAM Roles Anywhere X.509 certificate X.509 certificates

TIP context propagates to a new role session only under specific boundary conditions:

  • The target role is in the account where the identity provider is configured.
  • The target role is in another account within the same AWS organization.

IAM policies evaluate this identity context to authorize requests, and AWS CloudTrail records it for auditing. For example, Amazon S3 bucket policies and AWS Lambda can utilize this context for access control and audit logging. The identity context is represented through context keys, including the aws:OriginIdentity/* namespace, which serves as the common namespace for identity information across all three paths.

#AWS #IAM #CloudSecurity #IdentityManagement #CloudTrail #DevSecOps

Source: Know the identity behind the role: Authorize and audit with trusted identity propagation | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon Quick adds Smart Approvals for automated action review
item.description:
Amazon Quick adds Smart Approvals for automated action review

Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick addresses this challenge by reviewing eligible actions within your existing controls.

🔍 Overview

  • Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick reviews eligible actions within your existing controls.

🧩 How it Works

  • It evaluates each proposed action against the user’s request and either approves it automatically or returns it to the user for review.
  • Quick evaluates each proposed action against Custom Permissions, Quick Guardrails, connector action permissions, and the user’s settings before automated review.
  • With Smart Approvals enabled, an action is eligible only when the user’s setting is “Ask each time” and no other control requires human approval.
  • Smart Approvals uses a separate model, the classifier, to evaluate eligible actions against the user’s request and a bounded view of the conversation.
  • It can consult the user’s knowledge graph, which contains people and working relationships drawn from connected sources. This lookup stays within your Quick account.
  • Quick doesn’t use the content the classifier reviews, including knowledge graph data, to train models or improve the service.
  • Quick instructs both the agent and classifier to treat that content as information, not instructions.
  • Each automatic approval is single‑use, applies only to the exact action and parameters reviewed, and grants no ongoing permission.
  • Quick labels automatic approvals in the conversation.

⚙️ Permissions & Controls

  • Administrators use Custom Permissions to determine who can use Smart Approvals.
  • Connector action permissions, configured when a connector is created, can require human approval for specific actions.
  • It’s on by default, but profiles with deny‑by‑default enabled must explicitly allow it.
  • Users can also turn Smart Approvals off for themselves. That choice applies across conversations and scheduled runs.
  • When it’s off, actions otherwise eligible for automated review require the user’s approval, and no account‑level setting can turn it back on for them.

📜 Auditing & Logging

  • The Quick permission service records permission updates associated with Smart Approvals in AWS CloudTrail in your account.
  • Each event identifies the user, connector, action, and time, and marks the request as associated with Smart Approvals.
  • Quick also records permission‑check verdicts, including denials from connector action permissions, and changes to a user’s Smart Approvals setting.
  • Investigators can correlate these events by user and time with other Quick activity in CloudTrail and logs delivered through Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
  • CloudTrail Event history retains events for 90 days, so configure a trail for longer investigations.

🚫 What Does Not Get Approved

  • Actions the classifier doesn’t approve return to the user, as do timeouts and other review failures, which never grant automatic approval.
  • An approval to send to the original recipients can’t be reused for the wider audience.

#AmazonQuick #SmartApprovals #AI #CloudTrail #Automation

Source: Smart Approvals in Amazon Quick: Human oversight where it matters | Amazon Web Services
